title: Shift 2 Unleashed
text: I'm hard on racing games/sims but this is the best racing game I've played in a very long time.  If you enjoyed the first Shift, then you'll love Shift 2 Unleashed.  Shift 2 isn't a POS Need For Speed game.  It has great graphics, realistic racing physics, many cars to choose from, upgradeable and fully tunable cars and driving specifications, good for experts and beginners alike.  And get this..... You can use just about any game pad, controller or driving wheel you can think of and they're fully customizable.  This game doesn't suffer from the "rubber band" effect or cheating AI found in all Need For Speed games.  I've put about 35 hours into Shift 2 and I'm only about 60% complete with single player career mode and I've barely scratched the surface on multiplayer.  So, prepare to be challenged.  The only thing negative thing I can say about this game is that some of the endurance races are really long - almost an hour.  And that's not simulated time.  That's a real one hour race.  There's a bunch of them that make up a good chunk of the game just before the GT3 series starts and winning them is required to unlock the GT1 series.  So, you need to have some free time before you start one these races.

title: Shop Heroes
text: Absolutely addictive game (even though it's a mobile/FB game). Game basically goes like this: Caft an item, equip hero, send hero on quest, hero comes back with needed crafting materials, some items break, sell excess items to hero for exps or trade house for coins/gems, buy items for coins/gems. Rinse and repeat. They are constantly "re-balancing" the game. Meaning that they keep making it harder, upping requirements. I have yet to see them lower anything. While it's free, if you don't spend any money on it then you'll just be struggling all the time. It's primarily designed to entice new players. Once you hit mid to late game the game gets just utterlyslows to a crawl with 2+ hours doing anything. I believe I'm at mid game, quests taking around 7 hrs to complete, crating is at 2+hrs per item (not counting buildings). They offer premium packages with items that  that will lower crafting, questing, etc, but they're pretty much useless since they only do +/- 1% or 5%. I don't even see a difference in the amount of minutes/hours it takes to do anything. The onll really worth while premium package is the wizard package, once you can craft the Wisdom Ocarina and have a lvl 40 hero that you can sell to, life becomes easier. I didn't get this until lvl 40, i think most players quit around lvl 30, getting tired of the long waiting times. The whole game is designed to coax you out of every penny you have. I should also mention that at times there is just horrible lag where you can't do anything in the trade house or you're forced to watch automanted pvp battles as you're frantically hitting the skip fight button. Even at level 40, I'm discovering new things about this game. I could go on and on about the game, but then this review would take forever...... But it's very addictive and for now it's still somewhat fun. There are very few games on Steam that I would give a positive rating, too much half baked garbage.

title: Shovel Knight: Treasure Trove
text: I enjoy platformers; retro platformers to be specific...  Megaman 2, Super Mario World, Donkey Kong Country and so on.  I'm sure alot of people agree with me.  But why?  Why are retro platformers considered the best?  Is it the simple yet addictive gameplay?  The music?  the innovation for the time?  The nostalgia?  I tend to believe it's all of those things and it's something most modern platformers aren't getting right...  But, in 2014, came Shovel Knight!  A modern platformer in the style of 80s retro games!  It takes everything we know and love from our favourites and blends it into something new.  On top of that, it leaves out all of the flaws from those games as well!  It's like throwing:  Mario 3's world map, Megaman's robot master system, Ducktales' cane thrust and all sorts of other cool mechanics into one.  With the addition of Plague of Shadows and Specter of Torment, the game is now ten times better!  It's the same game with a twist on the gameplay and story, enough to make you wanna replay the game time and time again.  Now, that's exactly why I love Shovel Knight so much; it's all my favourite retro games in one great homage to the golden age of platformers! Everyting I love about platformers in one package

title: Shovel Knight: Treasure Trove
text: This review could be summed up as: GET THIS GAME NOW! For those of you who want a more elaborate exposition, Shovel Knight is a retro-styled platforming game from Yacht Club Games that has an incredible appeal in terms of design, gameplay and music. If you have had the pleasure of playing the original Mega Man series, then you'll feel right at home with Shovel Knight as the creators have spent as much attention to detail as the legendary teams behind that series on this game. Smooth controls allow you to fluidly turn a jump into a shovel-pogo on an enemy or bouncy obstacle and use the relics to chain in more awesome moves. The difficulty varies, but is challenging for both veterans and new players, the soundtrack is in a word spectacular in 8-bit style, where stages and bosses have their own theme, sometimes multiple ones. Aside from the main quest, there are so many optional bits, easter eggs and sidequests to dig into that you'll be astounded. I could go on for quite a while longer, but let me point this out: This game has proven such an incredible experience that even at full price it's the best buy you could make this year on Steam. Edit: Two years later and with the DLC campaigns added, its still awesome.

title: Shovel Knight: Treasure Trove
text: There's something very magical about this game. As of right now I'm 3 hours into it & already halfway through the Shovel Knight campaign and I can't wait to play the other 3 campaigns. Addicting gameplay, decent story, good humor, just an overall simple good time. It's the perfect mix of quite a few of our beloved nes classics and that's a beautiful thing. Let me tell ya, Shovel Knight may be heavily inspired by famed classics, however, it feels like something totally original. In other words, it's not too copy cat-ish. Everything about this game is enjoyable, nothing frustrating can be found here. My only complaint is that the bosses are a bit too easy. It's apparent that the developer didn't only make this game for retro platformers but newcomers as well. I recommend this game to anyone who loves classic platforming games... namely Megaman, Mario, Golden Axe or even the rpg known as The Legend Of Zelda.

title: Shovel Knight: Treasure Trove
text: Shovel Knight is fantastic.  It’s a rare sort of game that does things so right that even though I don’t usually like 2D platformers, I found myself in love with this spade-wielding hero.  The music is an absolute joy to listen to and the art and graphics are exceedingly charming and likable.  The game controls flawlessly and the level layouts are inspired.  And the whole package is wrapped up with a sweet, minimalistic story that was a joy to experience. This is the sort of game that I am happy I got to play.  It manages to be both accessible but deep, and I think it will be considered a staple of video gaming in years to come.  Needless to say, I would recommend Shovel Knight to anyone and everyone.

title: Shovel Knight: Treasure Trove
text: Looking for another fake retro game by lazy developers cashing in on oversaturated trends? One with immature memes, pointless obscure NES references, low-effort pixel graphics, and trial-and-error difficulty that'll make you pull your hair out? Good, then look at literally everywhere else, and stay away from Shovel Knight. Unlike the useless piles of Super Meat Boy clones and the uninspired puzzle platformers, this game does something that nobody has thought of before: it shows us the reasons we love retro gaming by removing all the things we hated about it. Take out the punishing difficulty, unintuitive physics, blinding-speed reaction times, tedious grinding, and ridiculously stressful objectives, and it turns out, yes, there’s still something left to love about the old games beyond masochism and nostalgia, something that was lost over the ages. Difficulty is not hard, but not easy; it's about just at the right level to feel satisfying when skill takes over. The controls and jump arc are simply perfect. There are tons of secret tricks that aren't explained, but will make you feel smart when you discover them yourself. Tough challenges become simple if you find clever ways to use your items. Graphics use the retro color palettes to great effect and can only be described as sweet, shiny eye candy, nothing like  the crappy MSPaint doodles you'll see in other pixel games. It's got powerful, energetic chiptune music that doesn't always make sense, but is catchy and gets you pumped to play -- every track is like some offspring of the Wily fortress music from Mega Man 2 and Castlevania 2's Bloody Tears. You can wreck enemies with the Downstab from Zelda 2, the Deluge from Faxanadu, the microphone from Kirby's Adventure, or even a fishing rod -- or sneak past them with invincibility, if you've got magic power to spare. Best of all, the challenges are rewarding and simply a joy to play from beginning to end -- you'll never feel afraid of what the game has in store for you, you'll just want to see more. And even if you die, you can even get your stuff back if you dare to try again. Believe the hype. As of now, I consider Shovel Knight the best fake retro game of all time. If you don't get why the retro fad is even happening in the first place, how so many gamers could possibly have such blind nostalgia for such old, technically inferior games with chiptunes and pixel graphics, this game might just show you why we all love retro gaming and why it will never go away. A rare 10/10!

title: Shower With Your Dad Simulator 2015: Do You Still Shower With Your Dad
text: I shall be one of the lame people who does an actual serious review for this game because.. Why not? I'll start off by issuing a warning that if you have epilepsy, take all games seriously or you just can't handle pixelated nudity then steer very clear of this, it's not for you. Developed and published by Marbenx, let's take a look at Shower with your Dad Simulator 2015. : As difficult as it is to write about; Shower With Your Dad Simulator 2015 is a series of actually challenging mini-games(e.g Endurodad, Dadathon, Dad Divisions, Soapia etc.), topped with pixely nudity, all kinds of dads and a rather addicting streak to it. : Extremely simplistic, but done in a decent way. The only thing that I dislike is that if you hit escape, the game will close on you. : Each mini-game has it's own soundtrack that is looped in a pretty non-annoying way even after a decent amount of play time, and it's actually good! : I found myself getting frustrated time and again over the curve-balls it will sometimes throw you. Something as tiny as a puddle on the floor will have you slide into the wrong dad and make you start over, or lose your streak(depending on which mode you're in). It's a nice challenge that by no means takes itself seriously and I think that's what I enjoy most about it. It keeps you trying that one more time to beat your previous score, that is the sign of a well put together game for entertainment. In all, I recommend it if you like simplistic yet fairly difficult games to keep you on your toes. Also if you like Showering with Dad simulators, nudity, showers and pixely goodness.

title: SiN Episodes: Emergence
text: This is one of those ancient by todays standard games. Released in 2006 but it feels like it been 15 years since I saw it on a demo disc from some gaming magazine with trailers. The controls are by todays standard pretty damn slow but it was back then pretty good, on par with the other Source engine games. The graphics was great too and the story was pretty good. It has not aged that well since it is super cheesy story it brought to the table and the Source engine is getting pretty old by now. It was probably one of the first companies, Ritual! To announce an episode based game with an trailer for episode 2 in the end of the episode im reviewing. The sad part is they probably had a bad time economically so this is a relic of the past, to show what it could have been. I have no idea who owns the license for Sin these days but I think the interest of making something with it is rock bottom. So this is something you should know if you ever look upon this and think, Hell I want an old fan servicey FPS similar to the olden days. The price is a steep one for how many hours you get. The complains I see is often about the episodes not being released or that the hours are to short but that is something you should know before you buy it. It is what it is, if you want a 30 hour campaign this is not for you. The foundation for an interesting episodic game is there,  the villianess which is a lot of TnA and a stereotypical slavic drug lord  for side kick works in this over the top world. It is a bit like playing the rowdy, moron cousin from the country of Half Life 2's. It is fun for a few hours, but do not expect a masterpieces and maybe see if you can get it on a sale if it ever goes on one. It is a look into the last decades "what could been" episodic content.

title: SiN Episodes: Emergence
text: I enjoyed the first SiN long time ago, so when I heard of this "sequel" I was very interested. Unfortunately this is the only Episode of this new chapter. SiN Episodes is an FPS based on Half-Life 2 Source engine, but while the phisycs ingame constantly provide some laughs for the usual odd and random "dead postures" I really missed one of the innovations from the first SiN: the armor system. But besides that the game is fine after all, there are cutscenes, a good music that follows and push the action (not to mention the Killer menu theme which I definitely love), the settings are very suggestive so we find the classic laboratories, sewers and now we see also a Dock, and a Huge building called "supremacy Tower". As usual there are a few minor bugs mostly temporary getting stuck between objects like chairs, or maybe gates that won't open because there are (or have been) some props over there. Nothing that a good jump or Checkpoint load can't solve. What this sequel miss in my humble opinion is the innovation of the first game, with ambience and computers interactions, the aforementioned armor system, stealth sections. This franchise had potential but it doesn't add anything particular or new to the genre. The story starts good, but the lack of explanations (supposedly postponed to a second episode that never came out) doesn't help much. This doesn't mean this title is bad, I mean: it's well designed, it starts with a good story and all and even though this Episode lasted quite longer than I could have expected it doesn't bring any innovation like its predecessor did. I remember being a huge fan of this game when videogames magazines with CDs full of demos were the thing. I'll be honest I just loved the Gun and the sniper rifle, their design was simply badass. However I've never been able to finish it, so when I found out that it came as a bonus with Sin Episodes: Emergence I thought it was a good chance to finish it once and for all... B-) SiN is a 1998 classic FPS based on the good old Quake II Engine. There are many little things that really hit me, both at the time and nowadays. The setting is the Freeport metropolis in a near future where police has been replaced by private security forces, which Blade (the protagonist) is part of. So we see modern/near future-like bank offices, laboratories, slums, sewers, a Dam and more. Besides the nice level design (especially for the times) there are some interesting elements like few drivable vehicles, usable computers with open-close commands and sometimes interesting prompt command menus, civilians and hostages which you need to save, a few stealth situations (optional, but still preferable). Still one of the most interesting and studied news is a well used Ghoul System, so now it actually matters shooting on a head or on legs. And that's not all because both you and enemies can wear bullet-proof protections and they are categorized according to the ghoul system, so you have helmet, jacket and pants which protect those parts. So As you shoot your enemies in different parts they might drop damaged vests. Very clever. The story isn't much the strong side of the game: in the aforementioned Freeport thre's a criminality escalation. A dangerous drug named U4 is spreading in the streets and the game starts during a Bank heist we must stop. Our "gunned investigations" will bring us to linking U4 to a big corporation that is producing it. Like I said it's not the most original plot, but the gameplay is leading the way As well as some polygonal fan service...

title: SiN Episodes: Emergence
text: Like the Half Life Episodes, I'm going to not recommend this game on the fact alone that the episodes were not finished. But as for the game itself, the graphics are okay, not quite as good as Half Life Episodes.  The game takes a while to get going as well, there's a good 10-15 minutes it feels of exposition/running around before you finally get a gun in your hands, that sort of introduction doesn't really fly into today's game market I feel. Gameplay wise, the player only has three guns with a primary and secondary mode in addition to a melee attack. This is admittedly very limited and the guns, being a pistol, shotgun and assault rifle are not particularly interesting.  The enemy variety is at times lacking with the bulk of the enemies being ordinary soldier guys of sometimes varying health with one of the three aforementioned weapons, in addition to that, we get some creepy crawly melee guys and some armored heavies.  In actuality the enemies do have some variety but most of the time it doesn't feel that way.  Gunplay is pretty solid, the guns are satisfying to use and the enemy animations when you take them out feel great.  They do try to add some new mechanics like, some noxious gas that gives you bullet time but I find it too fiddly to use. You'll also regain health mainly by medkits on the walls which can be refilled with medical-spray bottles, this works okay but can be fairly limiting and sometimes you have to search around for a refill. I've played this through once years ago, and recently played through about 2/3rds of it again but gave up being on too high a difficulty. It does however highlight one of the problems with these older games is that sometimes you can find yourself in a difficult encounter and simply not have enough health to get through it. Oddly enough, this is the same problem that prevented me from finishing the original SiN as well. So, on principle of not being a finished product (only one episode) I cannot recommend however if the price is right, knock yourself out.

It's a sin that there's so little content across the board (That and the game has super awkward (unsexy) female designs that objectify them in the worst most pre teen way possible.) I'm no prude, femenist, SJW or pathetic cuck but when a game gives you the opposite of a boner you know something is wrong as you groan and look over your shoulder to see if anyone has somehow been watching you silently, judging you the whole time as they shake their head reminding you that you should call your family and say you love them as you stare this♥♥♥♥♥♥game in the face. The character models could give Fallout 3 a run for it's money as these are the worst character models I've seen in a Source engine game since Contagion. Obviously the creators of an engine know how best to use it but it's shocking that a game can look this on the Source engine a whole two years after Half-Life 2 was released. Many other devs at the time put it to good use and recent titles like Titanfall (Didn't play it) showed the Source engine may still have some life in it yet. The people are wayyyy smaller than doors and all the original art assets (Non recycled HL2 props.) look too large or cartoony to match the world around them which already looks horrible. There's no cohesion. Hell the HUD looks like something that would appear on an ugly,outdated,out of touch Kindergarten website. I think it uses some font that's like comic sans too. The character designs are inconsistant,uninspired,dull and basically look like the one artist on staff gave up and put whatever he could on the screen to get paid and go home (I feel his pain). The story and voice acting is also awful which helps make and add to the feel that the game may have been going for. Worse yet is it's AI which is so badly bugged to hell even after a suppossed patch (Did they not even shoot their guns before?) that it should get a world record or something. The grunts (I don't remeber their names which is funny because they certainly know yours ) are probably the dumbest AI I ever have and ever will see. Better yet sometimes after you shoot them or they shoot you they will instantly forget that they have ever seen you actually saying things like "Damn it I know he's here somewhere!". But wait, While they are "smart" enough to use hand gestures to coordinate with their team they aren't smart enough to know how or when the right time to use them is. The only reason you'll remember who your playing as is thanks to the grunts shouting your name at you the one and only Blade. The dumb grunts are the most memorable thing in the game in fact as their unintentional stupidity has stuck with me even after all this time. I remember one enemy stuck in the ceiling with a jetpack. Another walked away slowly his back turned to me as I killed everyone around him. One said " " before getting killed by his teamate who promptly got stuck on a door. It will be remembered as that game you didn't own that breifly had a check box in Garrys Mod 9, having a surprisingly kick♥♥♥♥♥main theme and for bankrupting it's developer which is actually kind of sad though considering that games quality not unexpected.
